Purpose: Independent observational timing context for the STEREO-A compression and

INPUTS AND METHOD
Raw density/speed: observations/raw/original_stereo_a.csv, copied from the original
analysis_repro STA_COHO1HR_MERGED_MAG_PLASMA cache. Speed is km/s, density cm^-3.
Magnetic magnitude and proton temperature come from our separately downloaded and

solar-equatorial inertial longitude; no fixed observation-epoch spacecraft position.
The original source hash and prototype probe hash are in stereo_stream_timing.json.
No remote downloads or external-model simulation outputs were needed.

COHO labels hourly interval starts. Here an hourly mean is represented by its
center, stamp+30 minutes. Using the label instead shifts arrivals by about half
an hour, much smaller than the physical mapping uncertainty. The source epoch is
November 26 through November 30, 2025, inclusive days. We use the fixed equation

 ta = ts + wrap180(phi_comet(ta)-phi_STA(ts))/14.1844
         + (r_comet(ta)-r_STA(ts))*AU / v,

with days and measured speed converted consistently, iterating the actual comet
radius/longitude. No phase shift, speed adjustment, cross-correlation alignment,
or amplitude fit is applied. This follows a persistent COROTATING STREAM BAND;
it does not claim that one measured parcel moves sideways from STA to the comet.
During the fast samples the source-target solar longitude difference is about
27--30 degrees; the source and target solar latitudes differ by about1.4--1.5
 degrees. Using a fixed25-degree separation at the later XMM epoch is an earlier-
arrival approximation, not the same geometric calculation. Switching between the
proper solar-equatorial longitude and ecliptic J2000 longitude changes these
arrivals by at most0.223 hours; it does not explain day-scale differences.

INDEPENDENT OBSERVATIONS
There is strong compression followed by distinctly faster, hotter and less dense
wind. This is consistent with an SIR-like transition, but n/B/T alone do not
uniquely identify a pure SIR or exclude transient contributions.
- Density peak: November28 15:30 UTC hourly center, n=45.94 cm^-3, v=423.7 km/s,
  |B|=16.78 nT. The source timestamp is15:00 UTC.
- Magnetic peak: November28 23:30 UTC, |B|=19.84 nT, v=541.3 km/s, n=4.92 cm^-3.
- The first three consecutive hourly samples above600 km/s begin November29
  03:30 UTC center. The first three above650 begin November29 04:30 UTC.
- The observed speed reaches780.8 km/s on November30 18:30 UTC.
- For the45 samples above600 km/s, median speed is674.8 km/s, density2.73 cm^-3,
  temperature340000 K and |B|7.18 nT. Density16th--84th percentiles are1.66--3.46.
These values independently substantiate the compression/high-speed premise.

CONTEXTUAL ARRIVAL BRACKET
Source center           Measured v    Mapped comet time       Diluted n
Nov28 15:30(density max) 423.7 km/s    Dec04 12:26 UTC         12.07 cm^-3
Nov28 18:30(transition)  511.0 km/s    Dec03 23:30 UTC          2.56 cm^-3
Nov28 23:30(B max)       541.3 km/s    Dec04 00:01 UTC          1.31 cm^-3
Nov29 03:30(first >600)  649.7 km/s    Dec03 16:04 UTC          0.90 cm^-3
Nov29 04:30(first >650)  656.6 km/s    Dec03 16:24 UTC          0.88 cm^-3
Nov30 18:30(speed max)   780.8 km/s    Dec04 18:25 UTC          0.79 cm^-3

The earlier dense/slow samples(n>=10, v<600) span mapped arrival times from
December3 00:27 through December4 17:54 UTC. The fast samples(v>=600) span
December3 16:04 through December5 06:07 UTC. Thus a compressed transition and
rising fast stream in the comet's longitude band broadly overlap the December3--4
XMM epoch. The first sustained fast tail from the actual measured speeds maps
around December3 afternoon, rather than a uniquely established December3 00--05
arrival. Earlier compression can map near December3 00 UTC, so a broad day-scale
association is consistent even though the precisely quoted interface time is not
independently reproduced.

This is deliberately NOT a single-valued physical prediction:44 adjacent hourly
mapping steps reverse arrival order. Most clearly, the Nov28 slow density peak
maps AFTER the faster samples observed12 hours later. Fast/slow interaction,
compression and evolving band structure must resolve such overlap in MHD. Sorting
and connecting these samples would conceal the failure of independent ballistic
propagation. The plot therefore shows them as separate scatter points.

COMPARISON WITH OUR ACTUAL PROTOTYPE
Reference read directly: results/{d['prototype_reference_case']}/probe.csv; ID2 STA and ID0 comet.
No observed timings were used to shift the model.
At native STA:
- Model density maximum is8.88 cm^-3 at November28 03:00 UTC, versus observed
  45.94 at15:30. The model compression is much weaker and about12.5 hours early.
- Model first crosses500 km/s at November28 14:00 UTC, about4.5 hours before the
  measured sustained crossing; it crosses650 at November30 02:00 UTC, about21.5
  hours AFTER the measured sustained crossing. This is a broader model transition,
  not an error removable by one rigid phase shift.
At the comet:
- Model density peaks at2.805 cm^-3 on December3 09:00 UTC and then falls.
- Model speed crosses550 on December3 18:00,600 on December4 07:30, and650 on
  December4 19:30 UTC. The last crossing is about27 hours later than the first
  sustained650-band ballistic timing and occurs after the published XMM window.
These are useful diagnostics of timing/diffusion uncertainty, not proof that the
same uniquely identified observed structure is tracked by the prototype.

IS A FAST COMET WIND WITH n~2--4 PLAUSIBLE?
A rising500--650 km/s wind and density of a few cm^-3 are broadly plausible in a
compressed transition during this epoch. The measured transitional511 km/s sample
alone scales to2.56 cm^-3 near December3 23:30. Dense slow material spans diluted
2.69--12.07 cm^-3, providing material for a compressed interaction region.

However, the fully developed measured fast tail with n~2--4 AT STA must not be
copied to1.87 AU unchanged. Pure inverse-square expansion gives fast-tail median
0.711 cm^-3,16th--84th range0.429--0.927, full range0.348--1.189. Therefore n=2--4
at the comet is not a direct observational validation of an uncompressed fast
stream; it requires additional concentration or sampling the compressed flank.
The stream-band evidence supports a broad timing/physical plausibility check,
not the prototype's precise density, speed, SIR phase or numerical convergence.

+"""Shared completed-case selection for observation diagnostics.
+
+Explicit selection wins; otherwise results/reference_selection.json supplies
+reference_case, with the historical priority used only when no selection exists.
+No empirical calibration or simulation data are changed here.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+CASE_PRIORITY=("wide_fine","wide_medium","fine","medium","coarse","wide_coarse")
+NONPHYSICAL_EXPORT_CASES={"wide_movie","pilot","interrupted_wide_medium"}
+
+
+def safe_name(name):
+    if not isinstance(name,str) or not name or name in {".",".."} or Path(name).name!=name or "/" in name or "\\" in name:
+        raise ValueError("Case must be a single results directory name")
+    if name in NONPHYSICAL_EXPORT_CASES:
+        raise ValueError(f"{name} is an export/pilot case, not a physical validation reference")
+    return name
+
+
+def completed(root,name):
+    safe_name(name)
+    folder=Path(root)/"results"/name
+    return (folder/"statistics.json").is_file() and (folder/"probe.csv").is_file() and (folder/"probe.csv").stat().st_size>0
+
+
+def select_case(root,explicit=None,available=None):
+    root=Path(root)
+    allowed=None if available is None else list(available)
+    if explicit is not None:
+        case=safe_name(explicit)
+        source="explicit --case"
+        details={}
+    elif allowed is not None:
+        # Legacy --cases explicitly restricts candidates; no outside case is injected.
+        ready=[x for x in allowed if x not in NONPHYSICAL_EXPORT_CASES and completed(root,x)]
+        if not ready:raise ValueError("No requested case has completed statistics and probe data")
+        case=next((x for x in CASE_PRIORITY if x in ready),ready[0])
+        source="explicit --cases priority"
+        details={"requested_cases":allowed}
+    else:
+        path=root/"results/reference_selection.json"
+        if path.exists():
+            selection=json.loads(path.read_text())
+            if not isinstance(selection,dict) or not selection.get("reference_case"):
+                raise ValueError("results/reference_selection.json must contain reference_case")
+            case=safe_name(selection["reference_case"])
+            source="results/reference_selection.json"
+            details={"selection":selection,"selection_sha256":hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
+        else:
+            ready=[x for x in CASE_PRIORITY if completed(root,x)]
+            if not ready:raise ValueError("No historical priority case has completed statistics and probe data")
+            case=ready[0]
+            source="historical completed-case priority"
+            details={"priority":list(CASE_PRIORITY)}
+    if not completed(root,case):
+        raise ValueError(f"Selected case {case} is incomplete: require results/{case}/statistics.json and probe.csv")
+    if allowed is not None and case not in allowed:raise ValueError("Selected case is outside explicitly requested candidates")
+    return case,{"reference_case":case,"source":source,**details}
+
+
+def case_provenance(root,case):
+    safe_name(case)
+    folder=Path(root)/"results"/case
+    files={}
+    for name in ["run.cfg","metadata.json","statistics.json","probe.csv"]:
+        path=folder/name
+        if path.exists():files[name]={"path":f"results/{case}/{name}","bytes":path.stat().st_size,"sha256":hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
+    return {"case":case,"files":files}
*** End Patch"));
